# Weather now (`weather-now`)

Current condition icon, temperature, words and a detail line; a generic condition vocabulary.

Group: Home controls. Styles: `import '@mosaic-home/design-system/css/home';` (or `style.css`).

## Web API

`createWeatherNow` (types in `dist/web/home/weatherNow.d.ts`): `.mh-weather-now`: the current weather. An optional `__place` above; a tinted condition icon (`.mh-weather-icon`, decorative: the words say it), the `__temperature`, and `__condition` and `__detail` lines.

```ts
export function createWeatherNow(options: WeatherNowOptions): WeatherNowHandle;

export interface WeatherNowOptions {
  condition: WeatherCondition | null;
  temperature: number | null;
  /** Appended to the temperature (default "°"). */
  unit?: string;
  /** The source's own words ("Light rain showers"), shown instead of the generic word. */
  text?: string | null;
  /** A detail line ("Feels 9° · 5% rain"). */
  detail?: string | null;
  /** Where ("Hillside"), shown above. */
  place?: string | null;
}

export interface WeatherNowHandle {
  el: HTMLDivElement;
  update(options: WeatherNowOptions): void;
}
```

`weatherConditionFromText` (types in `dist/web/home/weather.d.ts`): Maps a forecast source's own words ("Light rain showers", "Mostly sunny", "Thunderstorms", "Overcast", "Mist") tothe vocabulary with keyword rules; null when nothing matches.

```ts
export function weatherConditionFromText(text: string | null | undefined, options: WeatherTextOptions = {}): WeatherCondition | null;

export interface WeatherTextOptions {
  /** Map "clear" to `clear-night`. */
  night?: boolean;
}
```

## Web example

```ts
import { createWeatherNow, weatherConditionFromText } from '@mosaic-home/design-system/web';

// A forecast source's own words, mapped to a condition for the icon and tint.
const text = 'Light rain showers';

const weather = createWeatherNow({
  condition: weatherConditionFromText(text),
  text,
  temperature: 9,
  place: 'Hillside',
  detail: 'Feels 6° · 80% rain',
});

document.body.append(weather.el);
```

## React example
